---
title: "The agent context & collaboration system"
subtitle: "Shared context, review notes, and tools for any agent"
---

Flux gives agents access to the same project files and editing tools as the app. Run
an agent in your preferred terminal or vendor app, give it the project's context, and
ask it to compose figures, write prose, or address your review notes.

The files carry the context between sessions. Your machine's `UserContext` folder
holds your background and standing rules; each project's `Context` folder holds its
goals, notebook, and project rules. The Flux app is the review surface alongside the
agent: figures, manuscripts, comments, and context-stamped feedback.

# Where everything lives

Run `flux config` for this machine's resolved paths.

**Machine level — `<FluxConfig>/`:**

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `Context/UserContext/` | `WHO-AM-I.md` (you) + `RULES.md` (your standing rules) + any files you add | **You** |
| `Context/FluxContext/` | The stock docs — the single canonical home of agent-facing Flux knowledge (doctrine, workflow, every verb, slides, python/uv conventions, Lighttable…). Re-synced on every Flux update with machine paths baked in. | **Flux** |
| `plot_library/` | Your **global plot library**: reusable plots (any folders) that every project's Plot gallery can insert under **Global**. `flux config` reports it as `plotLibraryPath`. | **You** (and agents you ask) |

**Project level — `<project>/Context/`** (scaffolded for new projects; healed into old
ones on first open, or via `flux context-init`):

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `Project/MISSION.qmd` | The charter: question, data, deliverable, scope | Co-owned — you have final say |
| `NOTEBOOK.md` | The project notebook: state, decisions + why, dead ends, session log | **The agent** — you read + comment |
| `RULES.md` | Project rules; recurring feedback gets promoted here | Co-owned |

Mission, notebook, and rules are **first-class Flux Paper documents** — they appear in
the document picker's Context group, and **margin comments work on them**: annotate your
agent's understanding or memory and it treats those threads as corrections. The
feedback ledger and provenance journal live in `.meta/`.

# The review loop (in the app)

- **Comments** on any document — threaded, anchored to exact text.
- **Ctrl+Shift+M** anywhere — "Note to agent": one line, automatically **stamped with
  what you're looking at** (figure/element/plot part, document + selected text, slide +
  beat). **Add to queue** saves the note. The buttons in detail: @sec-note-popover. When words aren't enough,
  **Ctrl+Shift+S** freezes the window so you can draw numbered arrows on it and the note
  arrives with the picture: @sec-annotate.
- Ask an agent to read both queues (`flux feedback`, `flux comments`), fix each item,
  and resolve it with a note — threads close live in your margin. When unsure, it asks
  *you* via a margin comment instead of guessing.
- **In the reader**: any external agent session can read the live paper, page, and
  selection through `get_reading_context`.
- **Ctrl+K palette**: open mission/notebook/rules, global rules, and Note to agent.

## The note popover: Add, Edit, Withdraw {#sec-note-popover}

The **Ctrl+Shift+M** popover saves context-stamped notes in the project's feedback
ledger (`.meta/feedback.ndjson`). Its header previews the context stamp, and the
footer counts the open notes.

- **Add to queue** (or **Enter** / **Ctrl+Enter**) records the note and closes the
  popover. You can collect notes as you walk through a figure or manuscript, then ask
  an agent to read them with `flux feedback` and address them.
- **Edit** puts a queued note back in the box, including its stamp and snapshot.
  **Add to queue** replaces it; **Escape** keeps the original.
- **Withdraw** takes a note out of the open queue. The ledger retains its history:
  `flux feedback --all` shows it as *withdrawn*. An agent that already read it can
  see why it disappeared.

As an agent resolves notes, Flux shows an **Agent resolved: …** toast.

## Point at it: snapshot & annotate {#sec-annotate}

Some feedback is about *pixels* — a gap, an alignment, a control you can't select — and a
selection stamp can't carry it. **Ctrl+Shift+S** (or the **Snapshot & annotate** button in
the note popover, or the **Ctrl+K** command) freezes the window under a drawing surface:

- **Drag** draws the current tool — **a** arrow (a plain click drops a short arrow at the
  spot), **b** box, **p** freehand pen. Every mark gets a **number badge**, so the note can
  say *"1 is too big, 2 should align with 3"*. **Backspace** undoes the last mark.
- **Enter** hands the picture to the note popover, which widens to show the crop at a readable
  size (the note is about that picture); your draft text is kept, and **Add to queue** saves it as usual. **Escape** cancels
  the overlay and attaches nothing.
- The picture is a **crop** around your marks (the whole window if you drew none), saved
  beside the ledger as `.meta/feedback/<note id>.png` when the note is added — never
  before, so a cancelled note leaves no file. Each mark also remembers the **element under
  its tip** (`header.toolbar > button "Gallery"`), so `flux feedback` prints where every
  number points even before the image is opened.

In a browser build there is no window capture; the overlay still records the marks and
their anchors, and the note says *no screenshot*.


# Design properties

- **Agent-agnostic**: context lives in plain files, and CLI/MCP tools expose the edits.
- **Durable**: notes and resolutions append to the feedback ledger.
- **Auditable**: the journal and notebook record work and its rationale.
- **Safe with several writers**: notebook session-log entries go through `flux note`,
  which appends under the same lock the app holds while you edit. Concurrent agents
  cannot overwrite each other's entries, and an agent write defers to your in-app edit.
- **Reusable preferences**: when you state a standing preference, an agent can propose
  adding it to `Context/RULES.md` for future sessions.

# Troubleshooting

- `flux: command not found` → `~/.local/bin` missing or off PATH (the shim installs
  there on first run); the full path always works — see [Installing Flux](../installation.qmd).
- A verb says `deferred: … is locked` → you're mid-edit in the app; the agent retries.
  That's the coexistence model working.
- Old project without `Context/` → open it once in the app, or `flux context-init`.
